title: dianthus sylvestris subsp. longibracteatus
intro: Dianthus sylvestris subsp. longibracteatus, commonly known as the woodland pink or grass pink, is a species of flowering plant in the carnation family (Caryophyllaceae). It is a perennial herb with pink flowers that have been used in traditional medicine for their health benefits, which include reducing inflammation and promoting wound healing. The therapeutic actions of this plant are attributed to its ability to exhibit antioxidant, antimicrobial, and anti-inflammatory properties, which may help to soothe skin irritations and promote overall well-being. The bioactive constituents of Dianthus sylvestris subsp. longibracteatus include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
